import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Identify strong univariate predictors
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'derived':
            continue
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        effect = abs(np.mean(x[y==1]) - np.mean(x[y==0]))
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(x[y==1], x[y==0], equal_var=False)
        effects.append((effect, abs(t_stat), fid))
    
    effects.sort(reverse=True)
    candidates = [fid for _, _, fid in effects[:20]]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = []
    for fid in candidates:
        x = feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)]
        correlated = False
        for kept_fid in keep:
            y = feats.x[:, feats.column(kept_fid)]
            corr = np.corrcoef(x, y)[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                correlated = True
                break
        if not correlated:
            keep.append(fid)
    
    # Select top features by effect size (at most MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = keep[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # For logistic regression, include all drivers plus potential interactions
    columns = drivers.copy()
    products = []
    
    # Add some interaction terms between top features
    for i in range(min(len(drivers), 3)):
        for j in range(i+1, min(len(drivers), 3)):
            products.append((drivers[i], drivers[j]))
    
    # Simple weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(drivers):
        loadings[fid] = effects[i][0]  # effect size as weight
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), 
                  products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
